```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Lee 2025 fitted two population PK/PD models to the same 24 adults on ECMO who
received a continuous infusion of nafamostat mesylate into the ECMO drainage
line upstream of the pump. Blood was drawn at the same times from two sites:
the patient's central venous catheter (the "patient model") and the ECMO
circuit at the oxygenator outflow (the "ECMO model"). Each site was fitted
separately with a two-compartment PK model and an indirect-response model in
which nafamostat inhibits the first-order loss of the activated partial
thromboplastin time (aPTT). The two fits are packaged as two models:

* `Lee_2025_nafamostat_patient` -- central-venous samples.
* `Lee_2025_nafamostat_circuit` -- ECMO-circuit samples.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lee_2025_nafamostat_patient"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2025.1541131>

```{r load-models}
mod_patient <- readModelDb("Lee_2025_nafamostat_patient")
mod_circuit <- readModelDb("Lee_2025_nafamostat_circuit")
```

# Population

The study enrolled 24 adults (17 male, 7 female) on VA-ECMO (n = 13) or
VV-ECMO (n = 11) at Haeundae Paik Hospital, Busan, Republic of Korea, between
July 2021 and October 2022 (Lee 2025 Table 1). Mean age was 60.3 years
(SD 12.1) and mean weight 70.3 kg (SD 15.7). The commonest primary diagnoses
were pneumonia (n = 10), cardiogenic shock or ventricular fibrillation (n = 4)
and trauma (n = 4); 7 patients were also on CRRT. Nafamostat mesylate was
started at 15 mg/h without a bolus and titrated to an aPTT of 40-80 s; the
individual profiles of Figure 1 show rates of 15, 30 and 45 mg/h. The ECMO
sweep-gas flow rate had a median of 3.75 L/min (IQR 2.5-5.5), which is the
centring value of the gas-flow covariate in both models. The PK analysis used
162 central-venous and 162 ECMO-circuit concentrations, and the PD analysis
95 aPTT values from each site.

The same information is available programmatically via
`mod_patient()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them. Inter-individual variability is reported in Tables 2 and 3 as a
percentage; footnote b of both tables gives the RSE "for standard deviation",
so the percentage is the standard deviation of eta times 100 and the variance
is (percent / 100)^2.

| `lvc` (V1, L) | 7.01 | 3.83 | Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q, L/h) | 350 (fixed) | 46.7 | Table 2, footnote a |
| `lvp` (V2, L) | 55.0 | 36.8 | Table 2 |
| `e_qecmogas_vp` (gas flow on V2) | -0.852 | -- | Table 2; Results equation for V2 |
| `e_qecmogas_cl` (gas flow on CL) | -- | 0.0999 | Table 2; Results equation for CL |
| `limax` (Imax) | 0.355 | 0.436 | Table 3 |
| `lic50` (IC50, ug/L) | 350 (fixed) | 581 (fixed) | Table 3, footnote a |
| `lkin` (Kin, s/h) | 47.5 | 50.6 | Table 3 |
| `lrbase` (Base, s) | 34.5 | 33.0 | Table 3 |

# Closed-form checks of the packaged parameters

Two deterministic checks tie the packaged typical values to statements in the
paper. Neither depends on a random draw.

**Distribution and elimination half-lives.** The Discussion reports
t1/2alpha = 0.54 min and t1/2beta = 19.7 min for the patient model, and 1.2
min and 51.4 min for the ECMO model. They follow from the Table 2 typical
values through the usual two-compartment eigenvalues.

```{r half-lives}
two_cmt_half_lives <- function(cl, vc, q, vp) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  disc <- sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)
  # minutes
  60 * log(2) / c(alpha = (s + disc) / 2, beta = (s - disc) / 2)
}
typ <- function(mod) {
  th <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
  exp(th[c("lcl", "lvc", "lq", "lvp")])
}
tp <- typ(mod_patient)
tc <- typ(mod_circuit)
hl <- rbind(
  patient = two_cmt_half_lives(tp[["lcl"]], tp[["lvc"]], tp[["lq"]], tp[["lvp"]]),
  circuit = two_cmt_half_lives(tc[["lcl"]], tc[["lvc"]], tc[["lq"]], tc[["lvp"]])
)
hl_pub <- rbind(patient = c(alpha = 0.54, beta = 19.7), circuit = c(alpha = 1.2, beta = 51.4))
data.frame(
  model = rownames(hl),
  alpha_model = round(hl[, "alpha"], 2),
  alpha_paper = hl_pub[, "alpha"],
  beta_model = round(hl[, "beta"], 1),
  beta_paper = hl_pub[, "beta"]
) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "t1/2 alpha, packaged (min)" = alpha_model,
    "t1/2 alpha, Discussion (min)" = alpha_paper,
    "t1/2 beta, packaged (min)" = beta_model,
    "t1/2 beta, Discussion (min)" = beta_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(row.names = FALSE, caption = "Half-lives from the packaged Table 2 values vs. the Discussion of Lee 2025.")
stopifnot(
  # beta reproduces to the printed precision in both models
  all(abs(hl[, "beta"] / hl_pub[, "beta"] - 1) < 0.01),
  # alpha is printed to two significant figures; the patient value computes
  # to 0.51 min against the printed 0.54
  all(abs(hl[, "alpha"] / hl_pub[, "alpha"] - 1) < 0.1)
)
```

**Steady-state concentration and aPTT.** For a continuous infusion into the
central compartment the steady-state concentration is `R / CL`, and the
turnover model settles at `aPTT = Base / (1 - Imax * C / (IC50 + C))`. The
typical-value solve below confirms both at the end of a 24-h infusion at
30 mg/h with the sweep-gas flow at its 3.75 L/min reference. (After the 6-h
infusions of Figure 3 the ECMO model is still about 0.5% below its plateau,
because its terminal half-life is 51 min.)

```{r typical-ss}
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = 30 * 6, rate = 30, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 8, by = 0.05), cmt = "aPTT") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(Q_ECMO_GAS = 3.75)
ev_long <- rxode2::et(amt = 30 * 24, rate = 30, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0, 23.99), cmt = "aPTT") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(Q_ECMO_GAS = 3.75)
typ_ss <- function(mod) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_long, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame")
  s[abs(s$time - 23.99) < 1e-9, c("Cc", "aPTT")]
}
th_p <- exp(rxode2::rxode(mod_patient)$theta)
th_c <- exp(rxode2::rxode(mod_circuit)$theta)
closed <- function(th) {
  css <- 1000 * 30 / th[["lcl"]]
  c(Cc = css, aPTT = th[["lrbase"]] / (1 - th[["limax"]] * css / (th[["lic50"]] + css)))
}
ss_chk <- rbind(
  patient = c(unlist(typ_ss(mod_patient)), closed(th_p)),
  circuit = c(unlist(typ_ss(mod_circuit)), closed(th_c))
)
colnames(ss_chk) <- c("Cc_solve", "aPTT_solve", "Cc_closed", "aPTT_closed")
knitr::kable(signif(ss_chk, 4), caption = "Typical-value solve at the end of a 24-h infusion vs. closed form, 30 mg/h.")
stopifnot(
  # 24 h is > 28 terminal half-lives in both models, so the residual
  # approach term is < 1e-8 and the bound is set by the solver tolerance
  all(abs(ss_chk[, "Cc_solve"] / ss_chk[, "Cc_closed"] - 1) < 1e-3),
  # turnover t1/2 = log(2) * Base / Kin is about 0.5 h in both models
  all(abs(ss_chk[, "aPTT_solve"] / ss_chk[, "aPTT_closed"] - 1) < 1e-3)
)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation

Figure 3 of Lee 2025 shows median concentration and aPTT from 2,000 virtual
patients per model over a 6-h infusion at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 mg/h. Here
each model is simulated with 200 virtual patients per infusion rate, with
between-subject and residual variability. The paper does not say how the
sweep-gas flow covariate was set for the simulation; it is held at the
3.75 L/min cohort median.

```{r cohort}
rates <- c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50)
n_per_arm <- 200L
obs_times <- seq(0, 8, by = 0.05)

make_arm <- function(rate_mgh, n, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  label <- paste(rate_mgh, "mg/h")
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = rate_mgh * 6, rate = rate_mgh,
    cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, cmt = "aPTT")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Q_ECMO_GAS = 3.75, dose_rate = label) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(rates), function(i) {
  make_arm(rates[i], n_per_arm, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250521)
sim_one <- function(mod, label) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "dose_rate", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = label)
}
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_one(mod_patient, "Patient model"),
  sim_one(mod_circuit, "ECMO model")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_rate = factor(dose_rate, levels = paste(rates, "mg/h")))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$dose_rate), nlevels(droplevels(sim$dose_rate)) == length(rates))
```

# Replicate Figure 3

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 7}
fig3 <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(model, dose_rate, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Concentration (ug/L)` = median(Cc),
    `aPTT (s)` = median(aPTT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Concentration (ug/L)`, `aPTT (s)`), names_to = "output", values_to = "median")
ggplot(fig3, aes(time, median, colour = dose_rate)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(output ~ model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Median of 200 virtual patients", colour = "Infusion rate",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Lee 2025 with the parameters of Tables 2 and 3."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure 3 concentrations do not follow from Table 2

The aPTT panels above resemble Figure 3, but the concentration plateaus do not.
The paper's text reports a median steady-state concentration at 30 mg/h of
about 88 ug/L in the patient model and about 600 ug/L in the ECMO model; with
the Table 2 clearances the plateau is `R / CL` = 159 ug/L and 352 ug/L. The
mismatch runs in opposite directions in the two models, so it is not a unit or
salt-form factor (salt-to-base conversion would lower both).

The plateaus in Figure 3 are instead reproduced, for every infusion rate and
both models, by `R / Q`: the Figure 3 simulation appears to have used the
intercompartmental clearance (350 and 46.7 L/h) in place of the clearance
(189 and 85.2 L/h). Table 2 as printed is supported by everything else in the
paper: the Results text quotes CL = 189 and 85.2 L/h; the Discussion
half-lives above reproduce only with the Table 2 assignment (with CL and Q
exchanged the ECMO t1/2beta becomes 53.0 min instead of the printed 51.4); and
the observed circuit concentrations of Figure 1 at the 15 mg/h starting rate,
mostly 80-250 ug/L, bracket `R / CL` = 176 ug/L and lie below `R / Q` =
321 ug/L. (The central-venous observations at 15 mg/h, mostly 20-100 ug/L,
are compatible with either 79 or 43 ug/L.) The packaged models therefore keep
Table 2 as printed.

The plateau values below were read from Figure 3 by the maintainers (the
30 mg/h values are the ones stated in the Results text).

```{r figure-3-plateaus}
fig3_read <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model, ~rate, ~css_fig3,
  "Patient model", 10, 30,
  "Patient model", 20, 57,
  "Patient model", 30, 88,
  "Patient model", 40, 119,
  "Patient model", 50, 145,
  "ECMO model", 10, 205,
  "ECMO model", 20, 435,
  "ECMO model", 30, 600,
  "ECMO model", 40, 790,
  "ECMO model", 50, 1030
)
pk_typ <- tibble::tibble(
  model = c("Patient model", "ECMO model"),
  cl = c(th_p[["lcl"]], th_c[["lcl"]]),
  q = c(th_p[["lq"]], th_c[["lq"]])
)
plateau <- fig3_read |>
  dplyr::left_join(pk_typ, by = "model") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    css_table2 = 1000 * rate / cl,
    css_swapped = 1000 * rate / q,
    ratio_table2 = css_table2 / css_fig3,
    ratio_swapped = css_swapped / css_fig3
  )
plateau |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    model, rate,
    css_fig3, css_table2 = round(css_table2), css_swapped = round(css_swapped)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "Rate (mg/h)" = rate,
    "Figure 3 plateau (ug/L)" = css_fig3,
    "R / CL, Table 2 (ug/L)" = css_table2,
    "R / Q (ug/L)" = css_swapped
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state concentration: Figure 3 vs. the packaged clearance and vs. the intercompartmental clearance.")
stopifnot(
  # R / Q reproduces every Figure 3 plateau to within the reading precision
  all(abs(plateau$ratio_swapped - 1) < 0.12),
  # ...and R / CL misses every one of them by more than 40%, in opposite
  # directions in the two models
  all(abs(plateau$ratio_table2 - 1) > 0.4)
)
```

The simulated median aPTT at 6 h is compared with the Results text below.
Because Figure 3's concentrations were simulated with a different clearance,
its aPTT curves are not an exact target either; the packaged patient model
lands on the stated 39 s, while the packaged ECMO model gives about 40 s
against the stated 43 s, consistent with its lower simulated concentration.

```{r aptt-30}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_rate == "30 mg/h", abs(time - 6) < 1e-9) |>
  dplyr::group_by(model) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cc = median(Cc), aptt = median(aPTT), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(model = c("Patient model", "ECMO model"), cc_pub = c(88, 600), aptt_pub = c(39, 43)),
    by = "model"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cc = round(cc), aptt = round(aptt, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "Simulated median Cc at 6 h (ug/L)" = cc,
    "Simulated median aPTT at 6 h (s)" = aptt,
    "Paper Cc (ug/L)" = cc_pub,
    "Paper aPTT (s)" = aptt_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "30 mg/h: simulated medians vs. Results section 3.3 of Lee 2025.")
```

# Effect of the sweep-gas flow covariate

In the patient model the sweep-gas flow lowers the peripheral volume, which
changes only the approach to steady state; in the ECMO model it raises
clearance, so the plateau falls by `exp(-0.0999 * (gas - 3.75))`.

```{r gas-flow, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
gas_levels <- c(2.5, 3.75, 5.5)
ev_gas <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(gas_levels), function(i) {
  ev_typ |> dplyr::mutate(id = i, Q_ECMO_GAS = gas_levels[i])
}))
gas_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_patient), ev_gas, keep = "Q_ECMO_GAS", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = "Patient model"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_circuit), ev_gas, keep = "Q_ECMO_GAS", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = "ECMO model")
)
ggplot(gas_sim, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(Q_ECMO_GAS))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Typical Cc (ug/L)", colour = "Sweep gas (L/min)",
    caption = "30 mg/h for 6 h at the Table 1 quartiles and median of sweep-gas flow."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
# plateau check on a 24-h infusion (the 6-h run above is ~0.5% short of it)
gas_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(gas_levels), function(i) {
  ev_long |> dplyr::mutate(id = i, Q_ECMO_GAS = gas_levels[i])
})) |>
  rxode2::rxSolve(object = rxode2::zeroRe(mod_circuit), rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, keep = "Q_ECMO_GAS", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(abs(time - 23.99) < 1e-9) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Q_ECMO_GAS)
stopifnot(all(abs(gas_ss$Cc / (1000 * 30 / (th_c[["lcl"]] * exp(0.0999 * (gas_levels - 3.75)))) - 1) < 1e-3))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. PKNCA is run on the simulated cohorts to summarise
the plateau (average concentration from 2 to 6 h, after steady state) and the
post-infusion half-life, and the plateau is compared with Figure 3. Every row
is expected to differ by more than 20% for the reason explained above; the
comparison is shown so the size of that discrepancy is visible next to the
simulated values.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(model, dose_rate, sep = ", ")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_rate)
dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dose_df |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste("Patient model", dose_rate, sep = ", ")),
  dose_df |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste("ECMO model", dose_rate, sep = ", "))
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, duration = 6)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(2, 6),
  end = c(6, 8),
  cav = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(cav = round(cav), half.life = round(60 * half.life, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Model, rate" = treatment,
    "Median Cav 2-6 h (ug/L)" = cav,
    "Median post-infusion t1/2 (min)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA summary of the simulated cohorts.")
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- fig3_read |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment = paste(model, paste(rate, "mg/h"), sep = ", "), cav = css_fig3)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "cav",
  units = c(cav = "ug/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated plateau vs. Figure 3 of Lee 2025. * differs from reference by >20% (expected; see text).")
```

The Cav medians track `R / CL` of the packaged models (the median of `R / CL_i`
equals `R / CL` for a log-normal clearance), so the starred rows are the
Figure 3 discrepancy, not a simulation artefact.

```{r nca-gate}
cav_chk <- nca_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = sub(",.*$", "", treatment),
    rate = as.numeric(sub("^.*, ([0-9]+) mg/h$", "\\1", treatment))
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pk_typ, by = "model") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = cav / (1000 * rate / cl))
stopifnot(
  # median over 200 subjects of R / CL_i: omega_CL = 0.613 gives a sampling
  # SD of the median of about 5.4%, so 20% is > 3.5 SE
  all(abs(cav_chk$ratio - 1) < 0.2)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Figure 3 is not reproduced as published.** Its concentration plateaus
  equal infusion rate / Q rather than infusion rate / CL in both models (see
  above). The packaged models keep Table 2 as printed, because the Results
  text, the Discussion half-lives and the observed concentrations in Figure 1
  all agree with it.
- **IIV scale.** Tables 2 and 3 give IIV as a percentage with the RSE
  footnoted "for standard deviation"; the percentage is taken as the standard
  deviation of eta times 100, so variance = (percent / 100)^2. The bootstrap
  intervals are percentile intervals and cannot distinguish this from a
  log-normal CV reading; under the CV reading the large values (Q: 243% and
  134%; Kin: 105%) would give much smaller variances.
- **ECMO-model IIV of Kin.** Table 3 prints 75.8% with no RSE and no bootstrap
  interval, and does not mark it as fixed; it is packaged as an estimated
  variance.
- **Zero variances.** The ECMO model's IIV on V2 and on IC50 are printed as
  0.000 (fixed); they are packaged as `fixed(0)` etas so the parameter set
  mirrors the table.
- **Table 3 row label.** The row "omegaEC50" is the IIV of IC50 (the model has
  no EC50); it is packaged as `etalic50`.
- **Imax above 1.** Imax carries exponential IIV as printed. A virtual subject
  whose individual Imax * C / (IC50 + C) exceeds 1 has a negative aPTT loss
  rate and an aPTT that rises without limit during the infusion. At the
  infusion rates of Figure 3 this needs an eta several standard deviations out,
  so it is rare, but users simulating much higher concentrations should check
  for it.
- **Sweep-gas flow.** The paper does not say whether the covariate was
  time-varying within a patient, nor what value its Figure 3 simulation used;
  it is held at the 3.75 L/min cohort median here.
- **Dosing site.** Nafamostat was infused into the ECMO drainage line upstream
  of the pump. Both models, as in the paper, treat the infusion as an input to
  the central compartment; the difference between the sampling sites is
  carried entirely by the separately estimated parameters.
- **Sequential PK/PD.** The paper fixed each patient's empirical Bayes PK
  parameters while estimating the PD parameters. The packaged models join the
  PK and PD layers in one model with independent etas, which is the
  simulation-equivalent form.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  or PubMed as of 2026-11-04.
